summary: APM feed s135_double is degraded: 24.2% duplicates (658/2714) and 2.3% TCP sequence gaps (57/2511) indicate aggregation without deduplication and broker/SPAN egress drops.

findings.root_cause: Traffic aggregated from two ingress sources (e.g., SPAN + TAP or dual SPANs covering same link) to single APM port without deduplication - same packets delivered twice within milliseconds, 24.2% exceeds 5% threshold.
findings.impact_on_tool: APM wastes ~24% of 10G capacity on duplicates, inflates transaction counts, skews latency/response-time calculations and can trigger false performance alerts.

recommended_fix.why: Enable packet-broker deduplication window before delivery to APM to suppress identical packets arriving via parallel paths while preserving unique traffic.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker egress oversubscription/buffer exhaustion or SPAN buffer drops causing TCP sequence gaps - 2.3% exceeds 1% threshold despite tool not overloaded, indicating drops in TAP/SPAN or broker forwarding to 10G APM port.
findings.impact_on_tool: APM sees incomplete flows with missing segments, causing incomplete transaction reconstruction, inaccurate latency and false retransmission/loss detection.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute load across additional APM ports or filter/slice unwanted traffic at broker to eliminate egress policing drops and deliver complete TCP streams; APM does not need full payload so slicing is also viable.
